running.q: When is my adult family home's annual license fee due?
alts: What month do I pay the AFH license fee?
What happens if I pay my adult family home license fee late?
afh annual fee due date
How much is the yearly license fee per bed?
running.a: Each year in the month the home was first licensed. If it is not paid when due, DSHS imposes remedies, and the license annual fee was the second most-cited adult family home rule in DSHS's October to December 2024 list, with 140 citations. The fee is $450 per licensed bed a year since July 2025, which is $2,700 for six beds, per DSHS in writing.

running.q: Can my adult family home go two years between DSHS inspections?
alts: Does a clean inspection record mean fewer DSHS visits?
How do I get my AFH inspected less often?
afh inspection every two years washington
Will DSHS give me notice before inspecting my adult family home?
running.a: Possibly. DSHS licensors make unannounced inspections at least every 18 months, with a statewide average of 15 months. A home with no citations on its last three inspections, and no violations from complaint investigations in that time, may go up to two years (RCW 70.128.070). Because visits are unpredictable, providers must stay in continuous compliance rather than prepare only when an inspection seems due.
running.pathTitle: Understanding DSHS Inspections & Compliance

running.q: Who can file a complaint that brings DSHS to inspect my adult family home?
alts: What is a complaint-based inspection for an AFH?
Can a family member's complaint trigger a DSHS visit?
afh complaint investigation dshs
Can my own caregiver report my adult family home to DSHS?
running.a: Anyone can: residents, families or staff. A complaint-based inspection is triggered when someone files a concern with DSHS, and these can range from minor administrative issues to serious safety incidents. They are in addition to routine inspections. Complaints go to DSHS Residential Care Services online or through the toll-free Complaint Resolution Unit at 1-800-562-6078.

running.q: What are the most common DSHS citations for adult family homes?
alts: What do AFHs get cited for most often?
Top AFH violations washington
What rules do DSHS inspectors write up most?
Most-cited WAC for adult family homes
running.a: In DSHS's most recent published list, for October to December 2024, the medication system rule was cited most (WAC 388-76-10430, 179 citations), followed by the license annual fee, notice of resident rights and services, medical devices, background checks, personnel records, evacuation drills, safety and maintenance, resident record content, and the medication log. Most are record-keeping problems that a consistent documentation system prevents.
running.pathTitle: Understanding DSHS Inspections & Compliance

running.q: Can I use bed rails for a resident in my adult family home?
alts: Are bed rails allowed in an AFH?
AFH medical device restraint rule
What do I need before putting a bed rail on a resident's bed?
Can bed rails count as a restraint in an adult family home?
running.a: Only with the right steps. Devices that carry a safety risk, such as bed rails, cannot be used as a restraint or for staff convenience, and need an assessment, informed consent, and a place in the care plan first. This medical devices rule was the fourth most-cited adult family home rule in DSHS's October to December 2024 list, with 106 citations.
running.pathTitle: Understanding DSHS Inspections & Compliance

running.q: How do I keep my adult family home ready for a surprise DSHS inspection?
alts: AFH inspection prep checklist
What should I self-audit before DSHS shows up?
How do I stay inspection-ready year round in my AFH?
Is there a mock inspection list for adult family homes?
running.a: Build self-auditing into normal operations. Set a recurring review schedule for assessments and negotiated care plans, medication records, caregiver qualifications and training, background checks, emergency drills, incident and mandatory-reporting documentation, water temperature, food storage, bedrooms, exits and alarms, required notices, and insurance and business records. DSHS publishes tables of the rules most often cited in inspections, which show where homes most often go wrong.

running.q: Do I have to show my adult family home's inspection reports to anyone who asks?
alts: How long do I keep DSHS inspection reports at my AFH?
Can a buyer or visitor see my AFH inspection reports?
afh inspection report public 3 years
Do previous owners' citations stay with my AFH address?
running.a: Yes. Each home must keep its last three years of inspection reports available to anyone who asks (RCW 70.128.080). DSHS says its online Locator shows limits and enforcement issued within the previous three years. Because a change of ownership brings a new license, a previous owner's record may not follow the address.
running.pathTitle: Understanding DSHS Inspections & Compliance

running.q: What is a stop placement order on an adult family home?
alts: DSHS stopped admissions at my AFH, what does that mean?
Can DSHS stop my adult family home from taking new residents?
stop placement afh washington
What comes after license conditions in DSHS enforcement?
running.a: It means the home cannot admit new residents until violations are corrected and stability is demonstrated. DSHS uses it when there is significant risk if admissions continue. It is the third step on the enforcement ladder, after license conditions and civil fines and before license suspension or revocation. Civil fines and stop-placement orders are reserved for higher-risk situations; most citations require correction rather than severe penalties.
running.pathTitle: Understanding DSHS Inspections & Compliance

running.q: How much can DSHS fine an adult family home?
alts: What are civil fines for AFH violations in Washington?
AFH civil penalty amount
How big is the fine for running an unlicensed adult family home?
Can DSHS fine me per day for a violation?
running.a: Under RCW 70.128.160, civil fines are at least $100 per day per violation, up to $3,000 per incident, and up to $10,000 for a current or former provider operating an unlicensed home. By law, fines become more severe for violations that are repeated, uncorrected, widespread, or a threat to residents.
running.pathTitle: Understanding DSHS Inspections & Compliance

running.q: How do I write a good plan of correction after a DSHS citation?
alts: My AFH got cited, what goes in the plan of correction?
What should I do after DSHS finds a problem at my adult family home?
afh plan of correction tips
Can I keep operating if DSHS puts conditions on my license?
running.a: Treat it as a real fix, not a writing exercise. Protect the resident first, make any required reports, begin correcting, and document the response. A real correction addresses what happened, which residents may have been affected, what was corrected immediately, what system will prevent it happening again, and how you will monitor compliance. For lower-level or first-time violations, DSHS can set license conditions, and the home may continue operating while corrections are made.

running.q: How does DSHS decide which classification a Medicaid resident in my AFH gets?
alts: Who assigns a resident's CARE classification?
What does the CARE assessment look at?
how is CARE classification determined adult family home
Can I choose the rate for a Medicaid resident in my adult family home?
running.a: A DSHS case manager completes a CARE assessment; the home does not set the price. CARE weighs cognitive performance, clinical complexity, mood and behavior, activities of daily living, and exceptional care criteria. It places the person in a group first, working from the highest group down, then assigns a sub-level from the ADL or behavior score. The result is one of seventeen classifications, which, together with the county, sets the daily rate.

running.q: What does Medicaid pay an adult family home per day in King County?
alts: AFH Medicaid daily rate 2026
What is the Medicaid rate for adult family homes outside King, Pierce and Snohomish?
How much does DSHS pay per resident per day?
adult family home medicaid rates july 2026
running.a: It depends on the resident's classification. For rates effective July 1, 2026, the base adult family home rate in King, Pierce and Snohomish counties runs from $144.47 to $279.30 per day; in all other Washington counties it runs from $132.49 to $250.61. For example, D Med-High pays $225.32 in those three counties. These are base rates only, without add-ons, and they change each July 1 and sometimes January 1.
running.pathTitle: A Through E: How CARE Classifications Set an Adult Family Home's Medicaid Income

running.q: Are higher-classification Medicaid residents more profitable for my adult family home?
alts: Should I fill my AFH with D and E residents?
Is a D or E resident worth more to an adult family home?
high acuity residents AFH income vs cost
running.a: Not automatically. Higher rates are not free money: a D or E resident requires more staff time, more skill, and often more overnight coverage, so look at revenue and staffing cost together. Classifications also move, since residents are reassessed and a rate can go down as well as up. Income that depends on one or two high-classification residents is more fragile than the same income spread across six.
running.pathTitle: A Through E: How CARE Classifications Set an Adult Family Home's Medicaid Income

running.q: What ADL score puts a resident in C High, and what does it pay?
alts: How are sub-levels like Medium and High assigned?
What's the difference between C Med and C High?
CARE ADL score sub-level adult family home
How much does a C High resident pay an AFH?
running.a: Within a group, the ADL score generally sets the sub-level. In Group C, High is an ADL score of 25 to 28, Medium-High is 18 to 24, and Medium is 9 to 17. Group C means clinically complex without significant cognitive impairment. At the base rates effective July 1, 2026, C High pays $200.91 per day in King, Pierce and Snohomish counties and $181.93 in all other Washington counties.

running.q: Is CBHS Tier 3 money mostly profit for my adult family home?
alts: How much does a Tier 3 resident pay an AFH?
What do I have to provide for a CBHS Tier 3 resident?
cbhs tier 3 rate staffing
Does CBHS pay enough to cover one-on-one staffing?
running.a: No. Tier 3 pays $194.81 a day, about $71,100 a year, but it authorizes 6.1 to 10 hours a day of one-on-one staffing that has to actually be provided. At eight hours a day, that works out to about $24.35 per staffed hour before payroll taxes and overhead. The rates come from the 2025-27 collective bargaining agreement, in effect through June 30, 2027. Look at the payroll supporting the income, not just the deposits.
running.pathTitle: CBHS Tiers Explained: The Behavioral Health Add-On Behind Some AFH Income

running.q: What records do I have to keep for CBHS supportive supervision?
alts: Do I need daily logs for CBHS residents?
How do I document CBHS hours in my adult family home?
cbhs supportive supervision log
running.a: A daily log. To use Medicaid dollars, the Health Care Authority and managed care organizations need to verify that services were provided, so providers keep a log of supportive supervision for each day of service. Industry guidance is that the average hours delivered each month should line up with the resident's authorized tier. Eligibility is reviewed at least once every 12 months, and a resident who stabilizes may be moved to a lower tier.
running.pathTitle: CBHS Tiers Explained: The Behavioral Health Add-On Behind Some AFH Income

running.q: How does my adult family home get set up to be paid for CBHS?
alts: Do I need a contract with the managed care plans for CBHS?
How do I enroll my AFH for Community Behavioral Health Support?
cbhs provider enrollment providerone
Who pays CBHS to an adult family home?
running.a: Licensed adult family homes can provide CBHS as agency-contracted providers. A home enrolls through ProviderOne so that the Health Care Authority and the managed care organizations can contract with it, and it must contract with the managed care organizations to serve their enrollees. CBHS is administered by the Health Care Authority in conjunction with DSHS and began July 1, 2024, replacing the older BHPC wrap-around funding.
running.pathTitle: CBHS Tiers Explained: The Behavioral Health Add-On Behind Some AFH Income

running.q: What is IBSS, and can a resident have both IBSS and CBHS?
alts: Intensive Behavioral Supportive Supervision adult family home
Is IBSS paid differently from CBHS?
Can my AFH bill IBSS and CBHS for the same resident?
ibss vs cbhs
running.a: IBSS, Intensive Behavioral Supportive Supervision, is a managed-care alternative route to the same supportive supervision service as CBHS. The same tier and rate table applies to it. A resident has one or the other, never both, so they cannot be stacked for the same person.
running.pathTitle: CBHS Tiers Explained: The Behavioral Health Add-On Behind Some AFH Income

running.q: Can a resident in my adult family home get both SBS and CBHS?
alts: Do SBS and CBHS stack?
Can I get the SBS add-on for a CBHS resident?
sbs cbhs july 2025 rule
Which comes first, CBHS or Specialized Behavior Support?
running.a: No. For care plans from eligibility assessments on or after July 1, 2025, a resident must first be found not eligible for CBHS before receiving Specialized Behavior Support (SBS) under the Residential Support Waiver, so the two do not stack. That makes CBHS the state's primary route for paying behavioral support in an adult family home.
running.pathTitle: CBHS Tiers Explained: The Behavioral Health Add-On Behind Some AFH Income

running.q: How do ECS and SBS contracts pay an adult family home?
alts: What is the ECS daily rate for an AFH?
How much is the SBS add-on per day?
Is ECS paid on top of the Medicaid base rate?
ecs sbs rates adult family home
running.a: Expanded Community Services (ECS) is not an add-on: the home is paid the ECS daily rate ($256.87) or the resident's base rate, whichever is greater. Specialized Behavior Support (SBS) is an add-on of $178.00 a day on top of the base rate, for six to eight additional hours a day of individualized staffing. Both amounts come from the 2025-27 collective bargaining agreement. The home must qualify for and hold these contracts, and since July 1, 2025 a resident must first be found not eligible for CBHS before receiving SBS.

running.q: Can my adult family home still get paid for Meaningful Day?
alts: Is Meaningful Day still a specialty contract?
Why is Meaningful Day still listed on state pages?
meaningful day afh funding ended
Should I count Meaningful Day income?
running.a: No. You may still see Meaningful Day listed alongside ECS and SBS, including on state pages, but the 2025 state budget eliminated its funding. DSHS contracting staff confirmed in September 2026 that Meaningful Day has not been available since July 1, 2025, so it should not be counted as income.

running.q: Can I set my own private-pay care levels and prices in my adult family home?
alts: Who decides AFH private-pay Level 1 through 5?
Is there a state schedule for private-pay care levels?
how to price private pay adult family home
Do private-pay levels have to match other homes?
running.a: Yes. No agency sets private-pay care levels. Many homes price private-pay residents as a base monthly rate plus a care-level charge, often labeled Level 1 through 5, and each home defines its own levels and amounts in its admission agreement. Levels are reviewed whenever the home reassesses, and they are a business decision the next owner can change.

running.q: Does someone have to live in my adult family home?
alts: Is a live-in resident manager required for an AFH?
Can my adult family home run with shift staff and nobody living there?
can I hire a manager so I don't have to live there
running.a: Generally, yes. The rules require a qualified person to live in the home: the owner, or a resident manager when the owner does not live there, who is responsible for residents' care at all times. The one exception: no one has to live in the home if it has staff 24 hours a day and someone who can make decisions is always present (WAC 388-76-10040). A resident manager can be designated for only one home at a time.

running.q: What experience does a resident manager need for an adult family home?
alts: Resident manager qualifications washington AFH
How many hours of care experience does an AFH resident manager need?
Can a management company place anyone as my resident manager?
afh resident manager 1000 hours
running.a: Anyone serving as resident manager must meet the resident-manager qualifications, which include 1,000 hours of direct care within the past 60 months (WAC 388-76-10130). That applies even when a management company places the person in the home. The licensed owner keeps ultimate responsibility for all personnel issues (WAC 388-76-11060), so the owner must stay in charge of who is placed there. A resident manager can be designated for only one home at a time.

running.q: How soon can I open a second adult family home?
alts: Can I own more than one AFH in Washington?
AFH second license requirements
How long do I have to run my first adult family home before getting another?
multiple adult family homes washington rules
running.a: A second license needs 24 months on the first with no enforcement actions for significant violations; later licenses need 12 months since the last one (WAC 388-76-10037). Owning several homes yourself is a separate path from hiring a management company. A company can manage several homes under written agreements, but each licensed owner stays responsible for the home and its residents, meets with the manager monthly and visits at least quarterly, and each home needs its own on-site person in charge.

running.q: What should I ask an AFH management company before I hire them?
alts: Questions to ask before signing an adult family home management agreement
How do I interview a management company for my AFH?
afh management company interview questions
running.a: Ask whether they file the management agreement and form DSHS 27-226 with DSHS 60 days before starting; who will be the on-site person in charge and who employs them; what bond or insurance covers residents' money; what they report monthly; how many homes they manage; and what happens to staff and records if the agreement ends. Hiring a manager does not hand over the license: you stay responsible for the home and residents, meet with the manager monthly and visit at least quarterly.

running.q: What insurance does an adult family home need, and what should I look for in an agent?
alts: AFH business insurance coverage types
Can I take over the seller's insurance when I buy an adult family home?
adult family home liability workers comp insurance
How do I find an insurance broker who writes adult family homes?
running.a: An adult family home needs general and professional liability, property, workers' compensation for caregivers, and often abuse-and-molestation coverage. A buyer cannot take over the seller's policies, so coverage has to be placed before the change-of-ownership date. Look for an agent who writes adult family homes or assisted living, not just homeowners policies, knows which carriers will bind care-home risk in Washington, and can quote before closing. See Find a Professional.

evaluating.q: Why is it so hard to get a normal loan on an adult family home?
alts: Why won't my bank finance an AFH like a regular house?
AFH financing hard why
Is an adult family home a residential or commercial loan?
Why do lenders treat an adult family home differently from a home purchase?
evaluating.a: Because an adult family home is a house that runs a licensed business, it falls in a gap between two kinds of lending. Many residential lenders treat the care business as commercial use and decline, or will not count its revenue as your income. Commercial lenders lend on business terms: shorter loans, bigger down payments, and no financing for the license, contracts and residents a seller charges for. The SBA programs exist to fill that gap.
evaluating.pathTitle: How to Finance an Adult Family Home in Washington

evaluating.q: Can I use a regular home mortgage if I'm going to live in the adult family home and run it myself?
alts: Owner-occupied mortgage on an AFH
Can I buy an adult family home with a conventional loan?
I'll live in the house and run the AFH, can I get a normal mortgage?
Residential loan for an AFH I will occupy
evaluating.a: Sometimes. A handful of Puget Sound lenders write standard residential mortgages on licensed adult family homes when the buyer will occupy the home. It is the cheapest money and the lowest down payment, but you qualify on your own income and credit, the home's business revenue may count only partly or not at all, and it finances the house, not the business. The business portion is paid in cash or on seller terms. Use a lender that says it does this.
evaluating.pathTitle: How to Finance an Adult Family Home in Washington

evaluating.q: How much do I need to put down on an SBA loan to buy an adult family home?
alts: SBA 7a down payment AFH
Can an SBA loan cover the AFH business and the house together?
What does an SBA 7(a) loan pay for when buying an adult family home?
Minimum down payment to buy an operating AFH
evaluating.a: About 10% down is typical for an SBA 7(a) loan, according to the financing guide. Because the SBA guarantees most of the bank's loan, it can run up to 25 years with no balloon when real estate is the majority of the loan, and it can include the house, business, goodwill, working capital and closing costs in one loan, up to $5 million. The trade-off is a higher, variable rate and a slower close.
evaluating.pathTitle: How to Finance an Adult Family Home in Washington

evaluating.q: How long does an SBA loan take to close on an adult family home, and what are the catches?
alts: SBA loan AFH closing time
Do I have to personally guarantee an SBA loan for an AFH?
What are the downsides of an SBA 7(a) loan for an adult family home?
Why does my SBA lender want my tax returns and not my projections?
evaluating.a: Plan on 45 to 90 days with extensive paperwork, so get pre-qualified before you shop. Other trade-offs the financing guide lists: a guarantee fee added to the loan, a personal guarantee from anyone owning 20% or more, and underwriting on last year's tax returns, not projections. The rate is variable, set at Prime plus a spread.
evaluating.pathTitle: How to Finance an Adult Family Home in Washington

evaluating.q: What is the highest interest rate an SBA 7(a) lender can charge on an AFH loan?
alts: SBA 7a rate cap 2026
Is there a limit on SBA loan interest rates for an adult family home?
What's the maximum SBA rate on a loan over $350,000?
SBA variable rate ceiling Prime plus spread
evaluating.a: SBA caps the variable rate at a base rate plus a spread that depends on loan size. With the WSJ Prime rate at 6.75% (as of September 17, 2026), the ceiling for a loan over $350,000, the typical AFH purchase, is Prime plus 3.00%, or 9.75%. Smaller loans have higher ceilings. That is a maximum, not a quote; strong files price below it. SBA publishes a separate table for fixed-rate 7(a) loans.
evaluating.pathTitle: How to Finance an Adult Family Home in Washington

evaluating.q: Can an SBA 504 loan pay for the adult family home business, or just the house?
alts: SBA 504 vs 7a for an AFH
What is the difference between SBA 7(a) and SBA 504 for an adult family home?
Fixed-rate SBA loan adult family home real estate
Does a 504 loan cover goodwill or working capital?
evaluating.a: Just the real estate. An SBA 504 loan pairs a bank loan with a fixed-rate loan from a Certified Development Company, with about 10% down. The CDC portion is fixed for 25 years at a rate set off Treasury yields, cheaper than 7(a). But the business, goodwill and working capital are excluded, so the business is paid in cash or on seller terms, and there are two lenders and two closings. A 7(a) loan can include the business.
evaluating.pathTitle: How to Finance an Adult Family Home in Washington

evaluating.q: How much down payment does an investor need to buy an adult family home?
alts: Commercial loan on an AFH down payment
Portfolio loan adult family home investor terms
I won't run the AFH myself, how do I finance it?
Buying a second adult family home, what kind of loan?
evaluating.a: Usually much more than an owner-occupant. Banks lending on their own balance sheet treat an AFH as commercial property: typically 25 to 35% down (one local lender publishes a 70% maximum loan-to-value), 5- to 10-year terms with a balloon, amortized over 15 to 20 years, real estate only. These loans suit investors, experienced operators adding homes, and buyers who need speed or flexibility. The trade-offs are the most cash at closing and refinance risk when the balloon comes due.
evaluating.pathTitle: How to Finance an Adult Family Home in Washington

evaluating.q: What's the difference between the rate period, amortization and maturity on an AFH loan?
alts: What is a balloon payment on an adult family home loan?
AFH loan balloon refinance risk
My loan is fixed for 10 years but due at 15, what does that mean?
AFH loan rate period vs amortization vs maturity
evaluating.a: They are three different numbers. The rate period is how long the interest rate stays fixed, amortization is the years the payment is calculated over, and maturity is when the remaining balance is due. A loan can be fixed for 10 years, paid on 25, and due at 15; that last payment is a balloon, which means refinancing. For an AFH, the next lender will look at the license, occupancy and two years of income as they are then. Know all three before comparing rates.
evaluating.pathTitle: Can You Get a DSCR Loan for an Adult Family Home?

evaluating.q: What does debt service coverage ratio mean on an adult family home loan?
alts: DSCR meaning
What is a coverage ratio when buying an AFH?
How do lenders calculate DSCR for an adult family home?
What does a 1.50 debt coverage ratio mean?
evaluating.a: DSCR stands for debt service coverage ratio: the income a lender counts, divided by the loan payment. For example, $15,000 of monthly income against a $10,000 payment is a ratio of 1.50, meaning the income covers the payment one and a half times. The math is simple; what differs between AFH lenders is which income goes on top, so that is the first thing to ask any lender.
evaluating.pathTitle: Can You Get a DSCR Loan for an Adult Family Home?

evaluating.q: Will the AFH's income be enough for the bank to approve my loan?
alts: What coverage ratio do AFH lenders require?
1.25 DSCR adult family home
How does a lender decide if an adult family home can carry the loan?
Minimum net income to finance an AFH purchase
what DSCR do lenders want for an AFH
minimum debt coverage ratio adult family home loan
evaluating.a: It depends on coverage. Whichever loan type, the lender asks whether the home's income covers the payment. It takes last year's net operating income, after operating costs and, for a buyer who will hire staff, the wages to replace the current owners' hours, and divides it by the annual loan payment. Most want at least 1.25 times. It uses tax returns, not projections, and counts every loan on the deal.
evaluating.pathTitle: How to Finance an Adult Family Home in Washington

evaluating.q: Why does one lender say my AFH qualifies easily and another says it barely does?
alts: Gross income vs net operating income AFH loan
Do lenders count gross resident income or income after expenses?
AFH lender income gross net rent
Same adult family home, different DSCR from different lenders
evaluating.a: Because lenders count income differently. Some DSCR programs use gross income, everything residents pay before costs. SBA and commercial lenders use net operating income, resident income minus caregivers, food, insurance and other costs. Ordinary rental DSCR programs use market rent, and many exclude care homes. Caregiver wages alone often take a large share of what residents pay, so gross and net can be far apart. Ask which income a lender counts before comparing offers.
evaluating.pathTitle: Can You Get a DSCR Loan for an Adult Family Home?

evaluating.q: My AFH earns more now than last year. Will the lender use today's income?
alts: Two-year income average AFH loan
Does a recent increase in residents help me qualify for an AFH loan?
Whose income history counts when buying an adult family home, the seller's or mine?
Lender averages two years of AFH income
evaluating.a: Not necessarily. One Washington AFH lender described averaging two years of gross income documented by each resident's agreement, not beds filled today: a home that grossed $420,000 one year and $540,000 the next averages $480,000, even if it earns more now. SBA procedures for applications from October 1, 2026 use the last full year or a two-year average, and expected growth cannot be used to reach the minimum. Ask whose years count; for an established home it is usually the home's record, but lenders differ.
evaluating.pathTitle: Can You Get a DSCR Loan for an Adult Family Home?

evaluating.q: How do SBA lenders count an adult family home's income?
alts: SBA income test AFH 2026
Does SBA use gross or net income for an adult family home purchase?
SBA 1.25 coverage first business purchase
Can I use projected growth to qualify for an SBA loan on an AFH?
evaluating.a: On income after expenses, not gross resident income. Under SBA procedures for applications from October 1, 2026, a first business purchase needs income that covers all of the business's debt payments at least 1.25 times. The income is the last full year or a two-year average, and expected growth cannot be used to reach the minimum.
evaluating.pathTitle: Can You Get a DSCR Loan for an Adult Family Home?

evaluating.q: Why can an owner-operator get a bigger loan on the same AFH than an investor?
alts: Investor vs owner-operator AFH financing
Why does the lender subtract staff wages if I won't work in the home?
The seller nets $150,000, why does the lender count less for me?
Replacement wages AFH loan underwriting
evaluating.a: Because of who does the work. Most adult family homes are owner-operated, with the owners covering many care hours themselves. A buyer who will not work those hours must pay staff, so lenders subtract replacement wages before counting income. That means the same home supports a much higher price for an owner-operator than for an investor who hires staff, and a home that nets a lot to its owners may net far less to a buyer on paper.

evaluating.q: If the seller carries a note on the AFH business, does the bank count that payment too?
alts: Seller note adult family home DSCR
Does a seller-financed business loan affect my AFH loan approval?
Do lenders count every loan payment on an AFH purchase?
Seller financing and SBA coverage ratio
evaluating.a: Yes. The coverage test counts every loan payment on the deal, including the house, the business and any seller note, because they are all paid from the same income. Any loan on the license, contracts and residents is repaid from the home's income, so a lender counts it. Seller financing on the business can still help, since it replaces the buyer's most expensive loan, but it does not disappear from the math.
evaluating.pathTitle: How to Finance an Adult Family Home in Washington

evaluating.q: How much does the number of residents affect whether a buyer can get financing?
alts: Does occupancy matter for an AFH loan?
Empty beds and adult family home financing
AFH occupancy lender approval
Can two more residents get my AFH buyer approved?
evaluating.a: More than almost anything else. Each additional resident adds a full year of rate to the income while adding little to costs, because the house, license, insurance and base staff are already paid for. Two residents can move a home from a loan the lender declines to one it approves at full price. Lenders underwrite last year's tax returns, so the occupancy has to be real, not projected.

evaluating.q: What paperwork should I get from the seller before I apply for an AFH loan?
alts: What documents does a lender want when buying an adult family home?
AFH purchase due diligence tax returns resident roster
What should I ask an AFH seller for?
Buying an AFH what to request from the seller
evaluating.a: Ask for two years of tax returns and the resident roster with payer types, since that is what your lender will underwrite. Ask about the contracts: ECS, SBS and DDA contracts do not transfer on a sale, so confirm you can qualify for your own before you price them in. Ask for a price allocation between house and business, which decides what you can finance and how. Get pre-qualified in your loan type early; SBA loans take 45 to 90 days to close.
evaluating.pathTitle: How to Finance an Adult Family Home in Washington

evaluating.q: Do the ECS, SBS and DDA contracts come with the adult family home when I buy it?
alts: Do specialty contracts transfer on an AFH sale?
Will the seller's income hold up after I buy the AFH?
Expanded Community Services contract new owner
evaluating.a: No, not automatically. When an adult family home changes hands, the buyer applies for a new license, and ECS, SBS and DDA contracts do not transfer on a sale. Confirm you can qualify for your own before you price them in. Because of this, two years of the seller's income can overstate the first months under new ownership, which matters when a lender is averaging the seller's history.
evaluating.pathTitle: How to Finance an Adult Family Home in Washington

evaluating.q: Why should the AFH sale price be split between the house and the business?
alts: Price allocation house vs business adult family home
How do I finance the business part of an AFH?
AFH purchase allocation real estate business
Should the listing say how much is for the house and how much for the business?
evaluating.a: Because the split decides what can be financed and how. Residential and SBA 504 loans cover the real estate only, so the business portion is paid in cash or on seller terms, while an SBA 7(a) loan can include the business. Buyers are advised to ask for the allocation, and sellers to state it in the listing so each part can be financed correctly.
evaluating.pathTitle: How to Finance an Adult Family Home in Washington

evaluating.q: I'm selling my adult family home. How do I make it easier for a buyer to get a loan?
alts: What can a seller do if the AFH numbers don't work at the asking price?
Should I carry a note when selling my AFH?
Selling an AFH buyer financing tips
How do I price my adult family home for an SBA buyer?
evaluating.a: Price for the SBA buyer, who is most of the market; their lender underwrites your returns and occupancy. Fill empty beds before or during the listing, since every resident on the returns raises the approvable price. State the split between house and business, and consider carrying the business portion on seller financing, which widens the buyer pool. Know which buyer can keep your contracts. Lowering the price is the last lever, not the first.

evaluating.q: What should I ask a lender before choosing a loan for an adult family home?
alts: Questions to ask an AFH lender
How do I compare loan offers for an adult family home?
AFH loan checklist questions
What to ask a DSCR lender about an adult family home
evaluating.a: Ask whether they count gross income, net operating income or rent, and over what period and whose history. Ask their minimum ratio, down payment, credit score and cash reserves; whether the loan covers only the real estate or the business too; how long the rate is fixed, the amortization, the maturity, and whether there is a balloon; whether there is a prepayment penalty; and whether they lend the program themselves or place it with another lender.
evaluating.pathTitle: Can You Get a DSCR Loan for an Adult Family Home?

evaluating.q: Can I finance a house as a regular rental and then turn it into an adult family home?
alts: Do I have to tell my lender I plan to open an AFH?
Rental loan then convert to adult family home
Is it a problem not to mention the AFH to my mortgage lender?
Hiding AFH plans from lender
evaluating.a: The DSCR guide says never hide the plan. If you intend to run an adult family home, tell the lender. Financing a property as an ordinary rental while planning a licensed care home can conflict with the loan terms, the insurance, and the statements you sign. Many ordinary rental-property programs exclude care homes, so ask first.

evaluating.q: What does the AFH Occupancy & Financing Calculator show?
alts: AFH financing calculator how it works
Is there a tool to see if a buyer can get a loan on my adult family home?
Calculator for AFH coverage ratio by occupancy
Can a buyer get the loan at this price and occupancy?
evaluating.a: It tests whether a buyer could get the loan at a given price and number of residents. You enter the market, licensed beds, each bed's monthly rate, costs, buyer type (owner-operator or investor), price, financing terms, and whether the business is financed too. It shows the coverage ratio against the lender's requirement, results by occupancy, and the most a lender would finance. Results are working estimates, not a loan quote or an appraisal.

evaluating.q: How can I estimate the return on buying an adult family home?
alts: AFH ROI calculator
Cash-on-cash return adult family home investment
Cap rate and cash flow for an AFH purchase
I don't have the seller's P&L, can I still estimate AFH income?
evaluating.a: The AFH ROI Calculator analyzes cash-on-cash return, cap rate, net operating income and monthly cash flow from your own purchase, loan and revenue assumptions. If you don't have the P&L, a revenue builder fills in gross revenue by market and care level using private-pay ranges and the DSHS Medicaid rate. Count only beds with a Medicaid resident today; a Medicaid contract alone is not income. Results are estimates for planning only.

evaluating.q: A listing says the house is "AFH-ready." Does that mean it's a licensed adult family home?
alts: AFH-ready meaning
Is an AFH-ready house already licensed?
Listing says AFH ready, is it licensed?
what is the difference between an AFH-ready house and a licensed AFH
evaluating.a: No. "AFH-ready" is not "licensed." A listing can mean an operating home, a former one, a house that passed the building inspection, or just a marketing idea. When evaluating, start with the house and whether it will work as an adult family home, then the income it could earn, then what it is worth. The site's calculators use your own assumptions and give estimates, not appraisals.
